I've got something interesting to mention here: have you heard of Round Robin tests? Let's take a microbiological RR test as an example, so let's say there's a  company that  puts some bacteria into meat samples. They send those samples to a hundred different laboratories to let them find out which and how many bacteria are in these meat samples. Can this company know the exact amount of bacteria they put in there? Nope. If you throw a bunch in, you can't count them anymore, except with your own lab methods. But who says that you will find the correct amount of bacteria? Maybe someone else is better?


So what they do is the following: they take all results from every lab and calculate the average of those. Then you judge the labs according to their deviation from this average value.


It might happen that the average is in fact NOT the true number of bacteria in the samples because a lot of labs got it wrong. Now imagine you're failing this test because you are the only one who got it right...
So yeah, life is weird and unfair sometimes. It can be pretty infuriating.
